title: A shared registry step for SOS1 families: proposal to Noonan Syndrome Association (UK)

sentences.text: Our RASopathies Network supports SOS1 families; the atlas infers your SOS1 connection from your Noonan syndrome support, rather than an explicit gene listing.
SOS1-related Noonan syndrome and some RAF1-related disorders share overactive protein signalling, offering a reason to explore collaboration.
Their symptom similarity is atlas-inferred, with confidence 0.43—below 0.5—not proof that families have identical needs.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: PATRAS, the PATient-based Registry for phenotyping and therapy evaluation in RASopathies (EURAS), and our contact registry are potential starting points; their SOS1 coverage is atlas-inferred.
The Clinical, Genetic, and Epidemiologic Study of Children and Adults With RASopathies explicitly lists SOS1.
We propose sharing information about these resources, not assuming permission to share family records.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Before offering PATRAS to RAF1 families, let us confirm eligibility, registry stewardship and permission to circulate an invitation.
Please check whether a sunken lower breastbone and reduced clotting factor VIII and XI activity occur in RAF1 and KRAS families, rather than treating missing records as absence.
For PTPN11, please check reduced factor VIII and XI activity and gum overgrowth.
We must distinguish individual genetic changes: published RAF1 evidence includes both increased and impaired enzyme activity.
Let us jointly draft one short PATRAS invitation for RAF1 families this month, holding circulation until eligibility and the checks above are confirmed.
Which individual genetic changes increase activity, impair enzyme activity or cause loss of function?
We propose asking for a variant-by-variant table linking ClinVar records to published functional measurements, using ClinGen RASopathy specifications.
Dear Noonan Syndrome Association (UK),
I am writing on behalf of our SOS1 community to explore a small collaboration.
PATRAS is a promising starting point, although its SOS1 connection is atlas-inferred.
Would you help draft an invitation for RAF1 families this month?
We would hold circulation until eligibility and differences are checked.
Thank you for considering this shared first step.
[Your name], on behalf of RASopathies Network (RASopathiesNet USA / UK)
